steps.tx: The condition of **central precocious puberty** is true GnRH-dependent precocious puberty driven by premature activation of the hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal axis. It is defined clinically by the development of secondary sexual characteristics before age 8 years in girls (thelarche) or before age 9 years in boys (testicular enlargement >=4 mL). First-line medical therapy utilizes continuous depot **GnRH agonist** formulations (leuprolide, triptorelin) to desensitize pituitary gonadotrophs, halting pubertal advancement and preserving adult height.
steps.say: Central precocious puberty is GnRH-dependent, defined by pubertal onset before eight years in girls or nine years in boys. Sustained hypothalamic-pituitary activation leads to accelerated bone age and compromised adult stature. First-line therapy provides depot GnRH agonists to down-regulate gonadotroph receptors and arrest pubertal progression.

vis.caption: Tanner pubertal staging, hypothalamic axis activation, and epiphyseal closure. [Credit: StewardMD]

steps.tx: In contrast, **peripheral precocious puberty** is GnRH-independent, characterized by autonomous gonadal or adrenal sex steroid secretion without hypothalamic activation. Serum LH and FSH concentrations are suppressed, and endogenous response to exogenous GnRH stimulation is blunted. Causes include autonomous activating mutations in the **LH receptor** gene causing testotoxicosis (familial male-limited precocious puberty), feminizing or virilizing adrenal neoplasms, granulosa cell tumours, and **McCune-Albright syndrome**.
steps.say: Peripheral precocious puberty is GnRH-independent, characterized by autonomous steroid hypersecretion with suppressed basal and stimulated gonadotropins. Etiologies include testotoxicosis from activating LH receptor mutations, sex cord-stromal tumours, adrenal neoplasms, and McCune-Albright syndrome.

left.title: Central Precocious Puberty
points: Pubertal basal or GnRH-stimulated LH (>0.3 to 0.6 IU/L)
Responsive to long-acting GnRH agonist therapy

right.title: Peripheral Precocious Puberty
points: Suppressed basal and post-GnRH LH (<0.1 IU/L)
Refractory to GnRH agonists; treated with antiandrogens/aromatase inhibitors

steps.tx: The rare genetic condition **McCune-Albright syndrome** is caused by postzygotic somatic activating mutations in the **GNAS** gene, which encodes the stimulatory G-protein alpha subunit (Gs-alpha). The classical diagnostic triad comprises polyostotic **fibrous dysplasia** of bone, large cafe-au-lait skin macules with irregular jagged coast-of-Maine borders, and autonomous hyperfunctioning endocrinopathies, most commonly recurrent estrogen-secreting ovarian follicular cysts in young girls producing peripheral precocious puberty.
steps.say: McCune-Albright syndrome results from postzygotic activating GNAS mutations. It is characterized by polyostotic fibrous dysplasia, cafe-au-lait pigmentation with jagged borders, and autonomous endocrine hyperfunction, classically presenting as peripheral precocious puberty from recurrent autonomous ovarian cysts.

steps.tx: The benign variant **constitutional delay** of growth and puberty represents the most common etiology of delayed sexual maturation, occurring far more frequently in boys. Children present with short stature and delayed pubertal onset, accompanied by a delayed **bone age** that corresponds closely to height age rather than chronological age. Final adult height is typically normal, and family history frequently reveals delayed pubertal development in parents or siblings.
steps.say: Constitutional delay of growth and puberty is the commonest cause of delayed maturation, particularly in adolescent boys. It is characterized by short stature with delayed bone age that matches height age rather than chronological age. Final adult height reaches target genetic potential.

steps.tx: The formal diagnostic criteria for **delayed puberty** comprise the complete absence of breast budding (Tanner B2) by chronological age 13 years in girls, or failure of **testicular volume** to enlarge to at least 4 mL by age 14 years in boys. In addition, an arrest in pubertal progression lasting longer than 18 to 24 months between stages warrants comprehensive biochemical investigation to differentiate constitutional delay from hypogonadism.
steps.say: Delayed puberty is formally diagnosed when a girl lacks breast budding by age thirteen, or when a boy's testicular volume remains below four millilitres by age fourteen. A stall in pubertal development exceeding eighteen to twenty-four months also mandates thorough endocrine investigation.

steps.tx: The genetic syndrome **Kallmann syndrome** is characterized by congenital hypogonadotropic hypogonadism associated with complete **anosmia** or severe hyposmia, resulting from defective embryonic migration of GnRH-synthesizing neurons and olfactory axons from the olfactory placode into the hypothalamus. Testing reveals low circulating LH and FSH, subnormal serum testosterone or estradiol, and low serum **inhibin B**, distinguishing it from normal prepubertal states.
steps.say: Kallmann syndrome combines hypogonadotropic hypogonadism with anosmia due to failed embryonic migration of GnRH neurons and olfactory nerves. Circulating gonadotropins and sex steroids are low, accompanied by subnormal inhibin B levels, confirming defective gonadotroph axis activation.

left.title: Kallmann Syndrome
points: Associated with anosmia or hyposmia on testing
Disrupted migration of GnRH and olfactory neurons
Causal genes include KAL1 (ANOS1), FGFR1, PROKR2
Associated with bimanual synkinesia, renal agenesis

right.title: Normosmic Idiopathic Hypogonadism
points: Intrinsic defect in GnRH secretion or action
Causal genes include GNRHR, KISS1, TAC3

steps.tx: Isolated benign pubertal variations must be distinguished from true progressive precocious puberty. Isolated **premature thelarche** presents in infant girls under 2 years with non-progressive unilateral or bilateral breast development without pubic hair or growth acceleration. Similarly, isolated **premature adrenarche** presents after age 6 years with mild pubic or axillary hair from modest adrenal DHEA-S elevation without clitoromegaly or advanced bone age.
steps.say: Isolated premature thelarche and premature adrenarche represent benign pubertal variants. Premature thelarche features non-progressive breast budding in toddlers without growth acceleration. Premature adrenarche features mild pubic hair from early adrenal androgen secretion without virilization or accelerated bone maturation.

rows: Normal bone age, normal growth velocity
Sparse pubic/axillary hair, adult body odour
Slightly advanced or normal bone age
Breast, genitals, pubic hair, rapid height spurt

steps.tx: Loss-of-function pathogenic variants in the maternally imprinted and paternally expressed gene **MKRN3** represent the most common cause of familial **central precocious puberty**. The MKRN3 protein acts as a hypothalamic transcriptional repressor; loss of paternal expression lifts inhibition on the **kisspeptin**-neurokinin B-dynorphin (KNDy) neuronal network, triggering premature pulsatile secretion of GnRH and early pubertal activation.
steps.say: Loss-of-function mutations in the paternally expressed MKRN3 gene are the most common cause of familial central precocious puberty. MKRN3 acts as a molecular brake on hypothalamic kisspeptin neurons; loss of this repressor unleashes early GnRH secretion.
